mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the past three months signals an active monetary easing cycle, reducing discount rates for equity valuations and generating positive forward returns in the S&P 500 over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive in periods when FEDFUNDS declines, as measured by a t-test p-value > 0.05 or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the unemployment rate above 9.5% over a 3-month window signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which triggers a flight to safety and reduces equity risk appetite, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances where UNRATE exceeds 9.5%, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both residential construction (HOUST) and real personal consumption (RSAFS) indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint decline in HOUST and RSAFS fails to predict negative 60-day SPX returns, as evidenced by a Rank IC < 0.03 or a t-test p-value > 0.05 in walk-forward testing.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained drop in industrial production (INDPRO) below 92.0 for two consecutive months signals a contraction in real output, which increases recession risk and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when INDPRO falls below 92.0, as confirmed by a t-test p-value > 0.05 or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the CPIAUCSL above 218.0 within one month signals accelerating inflation, prompting expectations of tighter monetary policy, which increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns remain positive in more than 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL exceeds 218.0, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) and a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strong labor market recovery, boosting consumer confidence and corporate earnings expectations, which drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases > 100k and UNRATE decreases > 0.2pp in 1 month
failure_condition: The joint signal of rising PAYEMS and falling UNRATE fails to predict positive 60-day SPX returns, as shown by a Rank IC < 0.03 or t-test p-value > 0.05 in walk-forward analysis.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in real personal consumption (RSAFS) below 360,000 million dollars, combined with a drop in GDP (GDPC1) below 13,150 billion dollars, indicates a sharp contraction in aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue forecasts and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The dual signal of RSAFS < 360000 and GDPC1 < 13150 fails to predict negative 20-day SPX returns, as confirmed by a Rank IC < 0.03 or t-test p-value > 0.05 in walk-forward testing.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 93.0 for two consecutive months, combined with a rise in the federal funds rate above 0.2%, signals a supply-side contraction under tightening monetary policy, which increases cost pressures and reduces corporate profitability, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal of INDPRO < 93.0 and FEDFUNDS > 0.2% fails to predict negative 60-day SPX returns, as shown by a Rank IC < 0.03 or t-test p-value > 0.05 in walk-forward analysis.
